world.title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
world.description: Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8–10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems. A transition from continuous to periodic pulsed superradiant emission in coupled spin–resonator systems is demonstrated, revealing connections to time crystals and enabling synchronized microwave and optical frequency combs.
